ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: In the diagram, within circle $\odot O$, radius $OC$ is perpendicular to chord $AB$ at $D$. Point $E$ is on circle $\odot O$, with $\angle E=22.5^\circ$, and $AB=2$. What is the length of the radius $OB$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that $\because$ radius $OC\perp$ chord AB at point $D$,\\
$\therefore \overset{\frown}{AC}=\overset{\frown}{BC}$,\\
$\therefore \angle E=\frac{1}{2}\angle BOC=22.5^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle BOD=45^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \triangle ODB$ is an isosceles right-angled triangle,\\
$\because AB=2$,\\
$\therefore DB=OD=1$,\\
$\therefore OB=\sqrt{1^2+1^2}=\boxed{\sqrt{2}}$.

Therefore $OB=\sqrt{1^2+1^2}=\boxed{\sqrt{2}}$.
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is circle O, O is the center of the circle; AB is a chord near the lower side, OC is a radius from the center O downward to point C on the circle, and intersects chord AB perpendicularly at point D; E is on the circle, EA and EC are connected, and angle E is 22.5°, the problem gives AB=2. Reasoning: Because radius OC is perpendicular to chord AB, it bisects chord AB, so DB=AB/2=1. At the same time, a radius passing through the center and perpendicular to a chord also bisects the corresponding arc, so arc AC=arc BC. ∠AEC=22.5° is an inscribed angle intercepting arc AC, therefore the corresponding central angle ∠AOC=45°. Since arc AC=arc BC, ∠BOC=45°. Also because O, D, C are collinear, ∠BOD=45°. In triangle ODB, OD is perpendicular to DB, therefore ∠ODB=90°, and together with ∠BOD=45°, triangle ODB is a 45-45-90 triangle, OD=DB=1. Thus OB=√(OD^2+DB^2)=√(1^2+1^2)=√2.
